verdicts.note: IMSLP/Wikipedia: Au rouet, Op. 13 = Poème No. 2 for violin & orchestra (pub. 1911), violin-piano arr. by Ysaÿe.
IMSLP: Berceuse, Op. 20, F minor, solo violin with strings, flute and 2 horns; Schott Frères (Brussels) 1921, plate S.F. 5600, violin-piano edition. Wikipedia agrees (Op. 20).
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Divertimento, Op. 24 (comp. 1916, pub. 1921), violin & orchestra; violin-piano arr. by the composer.
IMSLP: Étude posthume, G major, solo violin (10 May 1886); printed Schott Frères (Brussels) 1989, ed. Jerrold Rubenstein, plate S.F. 9414; also Schole Music 2023. Wikipedia lists it without opus.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Fantaisie (Fantasia), Op. 32 (1925, pub. 1927), violin & orchestra; IMSLP alt. title "Divertimento No. 2".
IMSLP: Légende norvégienne, G minor, violin & piano (1882); printed in Henle HN 1201 (ed. Ray Iwazumi, 2021). Wikipedia lists it without opus.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Lointain passé (Mazurka No. 3) in B minor, Op. 11 (1889, pub. 1893); also in Henle HN 1201.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Les neiges d'antan, Op. 23 (Poème No. 5), D minor, 1914, pub. 1921.

IMSLP has only the 1920 holograph orchestral score (Juilliard manuscript collection); no printed edition found. Wikipedia lists the 1901 violin-piano original as "Petite fantaisie romantique". Manuscript-only.

verdicts.title: Poème nocturne, Op. 29 (violin, cello & orchestra)
verdicts.note: Poème No. 7 for violin, cello and orchestra; only printed edition is the violin-cello-piano arrangement (Éditions Antoine Ysaÿe, Brussels 1927, plate A.Y. 3447). The title note "(for violin and cello)" omitted the orchestra/piano, so the accompaniment should not be "Violin & cello" alone.

verdicts.title: Saltarelle carnavalesque in A minor, Op. posth.
verdicts.note: Op. 11 is Lointain passé (N7); IMSLP labels this one "Op. 11 (posth.)" and Wikipedia "Op. posth.". Only printed source is a 1970 Éditions Ysaÿe (Brussels) copyist score, parts are manuscript, so borderline for "published"; owner may prefer to drop it.

verdicts.title: Variations on a Theme by Paganini in A minor, Op. posth.
verdicts.note: Op. 12 in the IMSLP page title collides with the Poème élégiaque, Op. 12; Wikipedia/Boosey list it as "Paganini Variations, Op. posth." (on Caprice No. 24, 15 variations, c.1883, violin & orchestra). IMSLP has only holograph orchestral parts, but a printed violin-and-piano arrangement by Jacques Ysaÿe (Boosey & Hawkes, 1960; also Noten Roehr string orchestra 1994) exists.

IMSLP: Violin Concerto in E minor (c.1885-86) survives only as holograph manuscript (Royal Library of Belgium) plus an unofficial self-published piano reduction (Xiao, CC0, 2023); no published edition. Early unpublished concerto.

gaps.title: Sonate posthume, Op. 27bis
gaps.note: Sketch of the original "6th Sonata (à Quiroga)" found in the Lavergne manuscript, edited and completed by Graffin; IMSLP list also gives it as Op. 27bis. Borderline because the last movement is completed by the editor.

gaps.title: Grande Valse de concert in E-flat major, Op. 3
gaps.edition: Henle HN 1201 (ed. Ray Iwazumi, Urtext, 2021-22); IMSLP list: Op. 3, 1882
gaps.note: Composed during the 1882 Norway tour, dedicated to César Thomson; Henle rates its difficulty 6/9. Possibly a first edition.

existing_issues.issue: Dedicatee of Sonata No. 5 is Mathieu Crickboom (Wikipedia list; IMSLP dedication of the E-minor concerto also names Crickboom); "Crickx" appears to be a misspelling.
existing_issues.suggested_title: Sonata for Solo Violin No. 5 in G major, Op. 27 No. 5 ("Crickboom")
